name: Dahi ke Kebab
subtitle: crisp-shelled hung yogurt kebabs that dissolve into cream the moment you bite

ingredients.qty: 800g full-fat, hung overnight to give about 350g thick curd

ingredients.note: adds body so they hold shape

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp, dry-roasted until it smells nutty
4 slices, crusts off, blitzed to crumbs

prepNotes: Hang the yogurt in muslin overnight in the fridge with a weight on top. It must be dry enough to crumble, not spoonable — this is the whole recipe.
Roast the besan in a dry pan until it turns a shade darker and smells like toasted flour, then cool it completely before mixing.
Chill the shaped kebabs 20 minutes before frying so they set.

steps.text: Tip the hung yogurt into a bowl and mash in the grated paneer until smooth and even.
Squeeze the chopped onion in your fist over the sink to wring out its water, then fold it in with the green chilli, ginger, cardamom, white pepper, coriander leaves and salt.
steps.tip: Wet onion is the usual reason these kebabs fall apart in the pan.

steps.text: Work in the roasted besan a tablespoon at a time until the mixture just holds a shape when pressed. It should feel soft, almost too soft.
Rest the mix 15 minutes, then shape into 10 flat discs about 5cm across and 1.5cm thick with lightly oiled palms.
Press each disc into the breadcrumbs on both sides and on the rim, then chill 20 minutes on a lined tray.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee on a tawa over medium-low heat. Lay in half the kebabs, leaving space between them.
steps.tip: Medium-low. High heat browns the crumb before the inside warms and the kebab bursts.

steps.text: Fry undisturbed 3-4 minutes, until the underside is set and deep gold, then turn once with a thin spatula and give the second side 3 minutes.
steps.tip: Turn once only. Every flip after that is a chance for them to break.

steps.text: Drain briefly on paper, repeat with the rest, dust with chaat masala and serve hot with mint chutney.

storage: Eat them straight from the pan; they soften within the hour. The uncooked shaped kebabs keep 24 hours refrigerated on a covered tray and actually fry better cold.
